title: A Practical Upper Bound on Selection Bias Effects in Medical Prediction Models

problem.claim: Selection bias can impair the generalizability of machine learning models deployed in broader target populations, with potential harm in high-risk settings such as healthcare.

gap.claim: Existing methods for predicting model performance require unrealistic access to the target distribution or knowledge of the selection mechanism causing bias.

contributions.claim: The authors propose an upper bound on worst-case target-population model performance when the selection mechanism and target-population data are only partially observed.
The method is presented as a tool for estimating the impact of selection bias in otherwise intractable settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the proposed upper bound as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating the method's validity and practical utility using fully synthetic data, semi-synthetic data derived from the All of Us Research Program, and real-world selection bias in MIMIC-IV.

narrative_sequence.summary: Selection bias is common in real-world data and challenges model generalizability.
Deployment on broader target populations can cause poor generalization and real harm, especially in healthcare.
Practitioners need to assess model generalizability before deployment.
Existing performance-prediction methods depend on unrealistic distributional or selection-mechanism knowledge.
The authors propose a partial-observation upper bound and report evaluations across synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world settings.

source_observation.claim: The proposed bound is designed for settings where the selection mechanism and target-population data are only partially observed.

interpretation.claim: Robust pre-deployment assessment may be possible without fully identifying the selection process or target distribution.

application.claim: Practitioners could use partial-observation bounds to assess potential selection-bias effects before deploying models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, tightness, or failure conditions of the bound.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the bound's formal definition or assumptions.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, or performance improvements.
The abstract does not specify how partial observation is operationalized.
